records.prose: The 1117 output cap is a compensation element. LM1117 p15: minimum 10 uF if a tantalum is used, "the ESR of the output capacitor should range between 0.3 ohm to 22 ohm", 22 uF for the adjustable part with CADJ. AMS1117 p4 gives no ESR bound - only "part of the device frequency compensation", 22 uF solid tantalum "will ensure stability for all operating conditions", and without an adjust bypass "smaller capacitors can be used with equally good results". So 22 uF is conservative, TI's tantalum floor is 10 uF, and a FIXED 1117 has no adjust terminal. PROVENANCE: the window sits in LM1117 section 9, which opens (p14) with TI's note that these sections are "not part of the TI component specification" - guidance, not a guaranteed limit. CONSEQUENCE, restating the bound only: a candidate qualifies only if ITS OWN datasheet puts ESR inside 0.3-22 ohm; under 0.3 ohm it is outside the window. No source here states any dielectric family's ESR: "does THIS 22 uF part qualify" is a P3 part-slot question needing that part's datasheet, absent here. Why a floor exists is SLVA115A's mechanism (the loop needs an ESR zero); its p6 conclusion contrasts newer LDOs "inherently ceramic capacitor stable" with this older generation, where ESR "is very important to consider". INFERENCE: no 1117 page gives a frequency for 0.3 ohm; SLVA115A p2/p6 read ESR as the capacitor's minimum over frequency - the conservative reading, settled on a marginal part by ring count.

sources.note: Read verbatim - the output capacitor "must meet the required conditions for both minimum amount of capacitance and equivalent series resistance (ESR)", minimum 10 uF if a tantalum is used, "The ESR of the output capacitor should range between 0.3 ohm to 22 ohm", and a larger 22 uF tantalum when CADJ is used on the adjustable part; no measurement frequency is given anywhere on the page

Section 9 opens with the boxed Note read verbatim - "Information in the following applications sections is not part of the TI component specification, and TI does not warrant its accuracy or completeness" - which the 0.3-22 ohm window, Table 9-2, Fig 9-11 and Fig 9-13 all inherit; same page, 9.2.2.1.1 gives "A 10-uF tantalum on the input is a suitable input capacitor for almost all applications" and 9.2.2.1.2 the ADJ bypass rule 1/(2*pi*f*CADJ) < R1

The AMS wording read visually - the output capacitor is "part of the device frequency compensation", 22 uF solid tantalum ensures stability for all operating conditions, and 22 uF "covers all cases of bypassing the adjustment terminal" while "without bypassing the adjustment terminal smaller capacitors can be used with equally good results" - so 22 uF is the conservative figure, not a floor; no ESR bound appears anywhere on the page, and Fig 1 draws COUT as a polarized 22 uF part

Every ripple-rejection line, including the AMS1117-3.3 row (60 dB min / 72 dB typ at VIN 4.75 V), is conditioned on "COUT = 22 uF Tantalum, IOUT = 1 A" - the datasheet's own test capacitor is a tantalum, not a ceramic

The page behind this record's clause that a FIXED 1117 has no adjust terminal to bypass: pin 1 ADJ/GND is described as "Adjust pin for adjustable output option. Ground pin for fixed output option", so the CADJ bypass that raises the output-capacitor requirement exists only on the adjustable variant

Source of the frequency basis this record carries as an INFERENCE only - Fig 2 is the TPS76050 (PMOS/PNP-pass) region-of-stability chart of ESR vs output current, and its NOTE reads "The ESR used in these plots is the minimum ESR of the capacitor as ESR does vary over frequency", scoped by its own wording to those plots; the LM1117 has no equivalent chart

"The curve of this device requires that, for the minimum 2.2-uF of output capacitance, the ESR must be between 0.1 ohm and 20 ohm. Few capacitors have more than 2 ohm of ESR, so the upper limit on the ESR can usually be ignored" - the basis for treating the 22 ohm ceiling as nearly free; same page works the lower limit into fZ(ESR) = 72.3 kHz for 0.1 ohm and 2.2 uF

Read verbatim, and broader than the p2 NOTE this record also cites - "When designing with older linear regulators, ESR is very important to consider when selecting the output capacitor. As the ESR is a function of frequency, the minimum ESR is used in simulations. Newer LDOs like the TPS7A26 device are inherently ceramic capacitor stable" - stated for older linear regulators generally rather than only for the plotted charts, which is why the minimum-over-frequency reading is carried here as the conservative one

records.prose: A linear regulator turns the whole input-output difference into heat: PD = (VIN-VOUT)*IL + VIN*IG, continuous, at full load (LM1117 p18 eq 2-3). No layout choice reduces it - the only freedom is where the heat goes. In a still-air SMD design the path is junction -> tab/lead -> board copper -> air, so the copper attached to the tab IS the heatsink and its AREA is a first-class design variable: the headline theta_JA on page 1 of a datasheet is only the value for whatever copper the vendor's test board carried. Size it in this order (LM1117 p18 eq 4-5): PD; TR(max) = TJ(max) - TA(max); required RthJA = TR(max)/PD; then read the copper area off the vendor's own area table - noting that this whole procedure sits in LM1117 section 9, which TI opens (p14) by disclaiming as "not part of the TI component specification". Placement matters as much as area. TI measured 16 SOT-223 copper layouts in one cubic foot of still air (AN-1028 p3, Table 1 + Fig 3 - pads 0.0123 to 1 sq in, top only / bottom only / half-and-half): RthJA falls from about 110 to about 40 C/W with area, and putting ALL the copper on the component side is 10-15 C/W better than either other placement at equal area (p4 conclusions). Those absolute values belong to AN-1028's power-MOSFET test vehicle, not to a 1117 - carry the shape (area helps, top side wins) and take absolute numbers from the part's own table.

sources.note: Read the dissipation/sizing chain: eq 2-3 PD = (VIN-VOUT)*IL + VIN*IG with Fig 9-10 power-dissipation diagram, eq 4 TR(max) = TJ(max)-TA(max), eq 5 RthJA = TR(max)/PD, and the pointer to Table 9-2 as the design aid

The boxed note that opens section 9, read verbatim - "Information in the following applications sections is not part of the TI component specification, and TI does not warrant its accuracy or completeness" - and the sizing procedure this record cites (9.5.1.1 on p17-18) sits inside that section, so it is vendor guidance rather than a warranted spec

Where 9.5.1.1 actually starts: the heat path stated in words - junction -> die attach pad -> lead frame -> case -> printed circuit board -> ambient; Table 9-1 splits RthJC (component variables: lead frame, conduction pins, die size, die attach, molding) from RthJA (application variables: mounting-pad size/material/location, placement and SHAPE of the mounting pad, PCB size and material, trace length/width, adjacent heat sources, volume of air, ambient); Fig 9-9 cross-section draws RthJA = RthJC + RthCA with the mounting pad, a via and an extended copper plane on the far side

Table 1 gives the 16-layout matrix (layouts 1-6 top side 0.0123-1 sq in, 7-11 bottom side 0.2-1, 12-16 split half top / half bottom); Fig 3 plots junction-to-ambient thermal resistance vs pad area with three labelled curves - Top Cu lowest, 1/2Top+1/2Bottom next, Bottom Cu highest

Conclusions read verbatim - increasing pad area lowers RthJA from about 110 to 40 C/W over 0.0123 to 1 sq in, and "placing all the copper on the top side of the board further reduces RthJA by 10 C/W to 15 C/W when compared with the other two placements"; Fig 4 gives max steady-state dissipation vs pad area, ~1.3 W for the recommended 0.066 sq in layout

Test conditions behind those curves - 1 cubic foot still air, MIL-STD-883 / 750 method, 4.5 x 5 in 0.062 in FR-4 (0.29 W/m-C), 2 oz copper clad; B.1 shows the K-factor calibration is done on a power MOSFET, so the absolute RthJA values are that vehicle's, not a regulator's

records.prose: Why an older linear regulator names an ESR RANGE instead of just a capacitance. Its loop has three poles (SLVA115A Fig 1, p2): the dominant pole in the error amplifier, a LOAD pole set by COUT x RLOAD that moves with load current, and the pass-device pole from the pass element's parasitic capacitance. A three-pole high-gain loop cannot be stable, so it is compensated with a zero, and the cheapest zero available is the output capacitor's own ESR - fZ(ESR) = 1/(2*pi*RESR*COUT). Both ends of the window follow. Too LITTLE ESR puts fZ too high, so the gain crosses 0 dB at -40 dB/decade instead of -20: ringing, then oscillation. Too MUCH ESR puts fZ so low that the gain is still above 0 dB when the pass-device pole arrives. That is why this generation of datasheets plots a REGION OF STABILITY of ESR vs output current (Fig 2) rather than one number. Two practical consequences. The plotted ESR is the capacitor's MINIMUM ESR over frequency (note under Fig 2), so compare the window against the ESR at the capacitor's impedance minimum, not its 120 Hz value. And the test that settles it is a fast load transient: four rings or fewer means enough phase margin (p3-5 - a TPS76050 with 2.2 uF ceramic rings; the same cap plus 1 ohm does not). SLVA115A is written for PNP/PMOS pass elements - take the mechanism here, the numbers from the part.

sources.note: The three poles named and located - dominant pole in the error amplifier, load pole P(LOAD) formed by the output capacitor and load "and therefore varies with load current", pass-device pole from the pass element's parasitic capacitance - plus the statement that a three-pole high-gain system needs compensation and that using the output capacitor's ESR is the simplest and least expensive way to generate the compensating zero

Fig 1 open-loop gain plot read visually - dominant pole, P(LOAD) with its "Variation in R(LOAD) x C(LOAD)" arrow, fZ(ESR) with its "Variation in C(LOAD) x ESR" arrow, and P(PASS) near 1 MHz; the paragraph gives both bounds (ESR high enough that the crossing is -20 dB/dec, low enough that the gain is below 0 dB before P(PASS)); Fig 2 is the TPS76050 ESR vs output current chart with shaded Region of Instability under ~0.1-0.2 ohm and above ~20 ohm at CO = 2.2 uF; the NOTE states the plotted ESR is the MINIMUM ESR of the capacitor, as ESR varies over frequency

The window worked as numbers - "for the minimum 2.2-uF of output capacitance, the ESR must be between 0.1 ohm and 20 ohm", the lower limit setting fZ(ESR) = 1/(2*pi*RESR*COUT) = 72.3 kHz, the stable ESR-times-C product band, and "Few capacitors have more than 2 ohm of ESR, so the upper limit on the ESR can usually be ignored"; this page also carries the load-transient method - "Performing a load transient test and observing the amount of ringing on the output is the best way to determine if the capacitor selected is stable" - with Fig 3's MOSFET-switch jig, preferred to an electronic load because the transient is much faster

sources.section: Figure 4 - load transient with a 2.2 uF ceramic
sources.note: TPS76050 load-transient capture showing multiple rings after the initial spike = instability, with the text rule that four rings or fewer indicates sufficient phase margin

sources.section: Figure 5 - the same capacitor plus 1 ohm
sources.note: Same device and same 2.2 uF ceramic with a 1 ohm series resistor added: the transient settles without the ring train, i.e. ESR can be synthesized when the only available capacitor is below the window

records.prose: The 1117 minimum-load spec belongs to the ADJUSTABLE part. AMS1117 p3: the Minimum Load Current row (5 mA typ, 10 mA max, Note 5) carries Device = "AMS1117", the adjustable base, while every fixed suffix (-1.5 ... -5.0) is named on the Current Limit and Quiescent Current rows and NOT on that one; the p6 curve is titled "Minimum Operating Current (Adjustable Device)" (~6 mA at TJ 25 C, ~8 mA at 125 C, flat vs input-output differential). TI agrees independently: LM1117 p6 lists minimum load current only for LM1117-ADJ (1.7 mA typ, 5 mA max over temperature) and gives each fixed option a quiescent-current row instead. The fixed part is SPECIFIED at zero load - AMS1117-3.3 load regulation reads "VIN = 4.75 V, 0 <= IOUT <= 0.8 A" (p3) and the whole EC table header is IOUT = 0 mA; LM1117-3.3 is likewise 0 to 800 mA with line regulation at IOUT = 0 mA (p5). Mechanism: on the adjustable part the minimum load is drawn by the external R1/R2 divider (AMS p4 - "this current is normally the specified minimum load current of 10 mA"); on the fixed part that divider is internal (p5 - the top of R1 is Kelvin-connected inside). A FIXED 1117 therefore needs no external bleed resistor. Headroom: dropout is specified only to 0.8 A (Note 4, higher above it), 1.3 V max; TI's curve gives ~1.15 V at 500 mA / 25 C. A 5 V -5% rail leaves 1.45 V at VIN(min) - in spec, with ~150 mV of margin.

sources.note: Read visually - the Minimum Load Current row's Device cell says "AMS1117" alone (5 typ / 10 max mA) while Current Limit and Quiescent Current list the fixed suffixes -1.5/-1.8/-2.5/-2.85/-3.3/-5.0; AMS1117-3.3 load regulation is conditioned "VIN = 4.75 V, 0 <= IOUT <= 0.8 A"; Dropout 1.1 typ / 1.3 max V at IOUT 0.8 A; Note 4 says dropout is specified up to 0.8 A and is higher above it; Note 5 defines minimum load current as the minimum output current required to maintain regulation; Note 2 caps guaranteed dissipation at 1.2 W for SOT-223

The minimum-current curve is titled "Minimum Operating Current (Adjustable Device)" - flat at ~6 mA (TJ 25 C) and ~8 mA (TJ 125 C) across a 0-20 V input/output differential; no equivalent curve exists for the fixed devices
On the adjustable connection the current through R1/R2 "is normally the specified minimum load current of 10 mA" - the external divider is what supplies the adjustable part's minimum load

"In the case of fixed voltage devices the top of R1 is connected Kelvin internally, and the ground pin can be used for negative side sensing" - the fixed part carries its own divider, which is why the external bleed is unnecessary

Minimum load current is listed for LM1117-ADJ only (1.7 mA typ at 25 C, 5 mA max over 0-125 C, footnote 5 "the minimum output current required to maintain regulation"), while LM1117-1.8/-2.5/-3.3/-5.0 appear on the Quiescent current rows; dropout 1.15 V typ at 500 mA (1.25 V over temp) and 1.2 V at 800 mA

LM1117-3.3 output voltage specified "0 <= IOUT <= 800 mA, 4.75 V <= VIN <= 10 V", line regulation at IOUT = 0 mA and load regulation from 0 mA - the fixed variant is characterized at zero load, unlike the ADJ rows which start at 10 mA

records.prose: On 1117-class parts the tab is the OUTPUT, not ground - AMS1117 p1 pin connections (1 GND/ADJ, 2 VOUT, 3 VIN) with the TO-252 view labelled TAB IS OUTPUT, and LM1117 p3 Fig 6-1 (DCY 4-pin SOT top view) labelled "Tab is VOUT" with Table 6-1 giving VOUT as SOT-223 pins 2 and 4, pin 4 being the tab. Two consequences for the heat path. (1) The top-side heatsink pour IS the VOUT net. The generic advice - "put extra copper on the bottom of the board connected to the top pad by through-hole thermal vias" (AN-1028 p4) - is only available when the far-side copper is on the SAME net, i.e. a VOUT island; a via from that pour to a GND plane is a short, not a heat path. Vendor two-sided theta_JA data presumes the stitch: AN-1028 p8 says its two-sided boards carry 0.02 in plated vias between the planes. (2) The stitch is not needed to make the far-side plane work: AMS1117 p5 states the spreading layer need not be electrically connected and that the FR-4 couples the tab pad to a plane opposite or inside. So on 2 layers with a GND bottom the move is a large top-side VOUT pour with the ground plane continuous underneath it and NO vias through it; any bottom-side VOUT island is stitched only to its own net.

sources.note: 3-pin fixed/adjustable pinout read visually - 1 Ground/Adjust, 2 VOUT, 3 VIN - with the SOT-223 top view showing the wide tab as the fourth terminal and the TO-252 front view annotated "TAB IS OUTPUT"; the 8L SOIC view shows four VOUT pins, the same live-node heat spreader in leadframe form

sources.section: 6 Pin Configuration and Functions - Figure 6-1 + Table 6-1
sources.note: Fig 6-1 (DCY package, 4-pin SOT top view) is drawn with the tab labelled "Tab is VOUT"; Table 6-1 Pin Functions gives VOUT = SOT-223 pins "2, 4" and ADJ/GND = pin 1 described as "Adjust pin for adjustable output option. Ground pin for fixed output option" - so the tab is the output on every tabbed package in the family

"For maximum performance, it is recommended to put extra copper on the bottom of the board connected to the top pad by through-hole thermal vias", and the conclusion that top-side placement gives the best thermal performance - the stitching recommendation is the move that a live tab cannot make to a different-net plane

"For layouts with copper on the top and bottom planes, there are 0.02 inch copper plated vias (heat pipes) connecting the two planes" - the measured two-sided numbers include a galvanic path, so they may not be claimed for a VOUT pour over a GND plane

"Experiments have shown that the heat spreading copper layer does not need to be electrically connected to the tab of the device. The PC material can be very effective at transmitting heat between the pad area ... and a ground plane layer either inside or on the opposite side of the board" - the unstitched path that survives when the tab is a live node

records.prose: AMS1117 Table 1 (p5): theta_JA vs copper area, 1/16 in FR-4, 1 oz foil - min pad 90 C/W (p2); 1000 sq mm top + 0 back = 65; 1000 + 1000 back = 60; 1000 + 2500 back = 55; 100 + 2500 = 80 C/W. Footnote: tab attached to TOPSIDE copper. What is the back side connected to? Nothing. The paragraph above it states the spreading layer "does not need to be electrically connected to the tab of the device" and that the PC material carries heat from the tab pad to "a ground plane layer either inside or on the opposite side of the board". So the back-side rows are DIELECTRIC-coupled on ANY net: a VOUT-tab 1117 keeps them over a GND bottom plane. 55 C/W is no package floor either - the same page gives junction-to-tab 15 and tab-to-ambient as low as 30 C/W, i.e. 45 total on a well-coppered board. Cross-check LM1117 Table 9-2 (p18-19): top-only 0.0123 sq in = 136, 0.3 = 84, 1 sq in (645 sq mm) = 66 C/W - agreeing with AMS's 1000 sq mm -> 65, though all TI's numbers sit in section 9, which TI opens (p14) by disclaiming as "not part of the TI component specification". TI's two-sided rows are a DIFFERENT experiment: their split totals (0.132, 0.35, 0.568, 0.784, 1.0 sq in) are exactly AN-1028 layouts 12-16, whose boards carry 0.02 in plated vias (p8). No contradiction - TI SPLITS a fixed budget (Fig 9-11 ranks Top Cu best), AMS ADDS back-side area under a fixed top pour (~5 C/W). At TA 50 C even 55 C/W caps near 1.36 W: the envelope's 1.5 W marks where this record stops, never a licence.

sources.note: Table 1 read visually - COPPER AREA (TOP SIDE* / BACK SIDE) | BOARD AREA | THERMAL RESISTANCE, rows 2500/2500/2500=55, 1000/2500/2500=55, 225/2500/2500=65, 100/2500/2500=80, 1000/1000/1000=60, 1000/0/1000=65 C/W, footnote "* Tab of device attached to topside copper"; the paragraph above it states the spreading layer need not be electrically connected to the tab and that the FR-4 couples the pad to a ground plane inside or opposite, data taken on 1/16 in FR-4 with 1 oz copper foil; same page also gives junction-to-tab 15 C/W and tab-to-ambient as low as 30 C/W

SOT-223 theta_JA = 90 C/W with the asterisk footnote - "With package soldering to copper area OVER backside ground plane or internal power plane theta_JA can vary from 46 C/W to >90 C/W depending on mounting technique and the size of the copper area"; the wording again places the copper OVER a different-net plane rather than tied to it

The boxed note opening section 9, read verbatim - "Information in the following applications sections is not part of the TI component specification, and TI does not warrant its accuracy or completeness"; Table 9-2, Fig 9-11 and Fig 9-13, all cited by this record, sit inside that section and inherit it

Table 9-2 top-side rows for SOT-223 - 0.0123 sq in = 136, 0.066 = 123, 0.3 = 84, 0.53 = 75, 0.76 = 69, 1 = 66 C/W (TO-252 column alongside), and row 7 starting the bottom-only block at 0 top / 0.2 bottom = 115 C/W

Bottom-only rows to 0/1 = 79 C/W and split rows 0.066+0.066 = 125 down to 0.5+0.5 = 70 C/W (totals 0.132 to 1.0 sq in, matching AN-1028 layouts 12-16), with footnote (1) "Tab of device attached to topside copper"; Fig 9-11 (RthJA vs 1-oz copper area, SOT-223, still air, TA 25 C) shows three curves labelled Bottom Cu, 1/2 Top + 1/2 Bottom and Top Cu, Top Cu lowest across the whole sweep - note the figure says 1 oz while AN-1028's own board was 2 oz clad; Fig 9-13 on the same page plots max allowable dissipation vs ambient for SOT-223 per theta_JA curve (136, 123, 84, 75, 69, 66 C/W), the 66 C/W curve reaching ~1.5 W at TA 25 C and falling to 0 W at TJ 125 C - the basis for this record's pdiss_w bound

"For layouts with copper on the top and bottom planes, there are 0.02 inch copper plated vias (heat pipes) connecting the two planes" - the TI two-sided data assumes a galvanic stitch, which is what makes AMS's unstitched Table 1 a different (and for a live tab, the applicable) experiment

Mechanism: on the adjustable part the minimum load is drawn by the external R1/R2 divider (AMS p4 - "this current is normally the specified minimum load current of 10 mA"); on the fixed part that divider is internal (p5 - the top of R1 is Kelvin-connected inside). A FIXED 1117 therefore needs no external bleed resistor. Headroom: dropout is specified only to 0.8 A (Note 4, higher above it), 1.3 V max; TI's curve gives ~1.15 V at 500 mA / 25 C. A 5 V -5% rail leaves 1.45 V at VIN(min) - in spec, with ~150 mV of margin.

- linear-regulator-live-tab-thermal-vias [thermal-via] (topology/verified, workspace)
  On 1117-class parts the tab is the OUTPUT, not ground - AMS1117 p1 pin connections (1 GND/ADJ, 2 VOUT, 3 VIN) with the TO-252 view labelled TAB IS OUTPUT, and LM1117 p3 Fig 6-1 (DCY 4-pin SOT top view) labelled "Tab is VOUT" with Table 6-1 giving VOUT as SOT-223 pins 2 and 4, pin 4 being the tab. Two consequences for the heat path. (1) The top-side heatsink pour IS the VOUT net. The generic advice - "put extra copper on the bottom of the board connected to the top pad by through-hole thermal vias" (AN-1028 p4) - is only available when the far-side copper is on the SAME net, i.e. a VOUT island; a via from that pour to a GND plane is a short, not a heat path. Vendor two-sided theta_JA data presumes the stitch: AN-1028 p8 says its two-sided boards carry 0.02 in plated vias between the planes. (2) The stitch is not needed to make the far-side plane work: AMS1117 p5 states the spreading layer need not be electrically connected and that the FR-4 couples the tab pad to a plane opposite or inside. So on 2 layers with a GND bottom the move is a large top-side VOUT pour with the ground plane continuous underneath it and NO vias through it; any bottom-side VOUT island is stitched only to its own net.

- linear-regulator-tab-copper-area-theta-ja [thermal] (family/verified, workspace)
  AMS1117 Table 1 (p5): theta_JA vs copper area, 1/16 in FR-4, 1 oz foil - min pad 90 C/W (p2); 1000 sq mm top + 0 back = 65; 1000 + 1000 back = 60; 1000 + 2500 back = 55; 100 + 2500 = 80 C/W. Footnote: tab attached to TOPSIDE copper. What is the back side connected to? Nothing. The paragraph above it states the spreading layer "does not need to be electrically connected to the tab of the device" and that the PC material carries heat from the tab pad to "a ground plane layer either inside or on the opposite side of the board". So the back-side rows are DIELECTRIC-coupled on ANY net: a VOUT-tab 1117 keeps them over a GND bottom plane. 55 C/W is no package floor either - the same page gives junction-to-tab 15 and tab-to-ambient as low as 30 C/W, i.e. 45 total on a well-coppered board. Cross-check LM1117 Table 9-2 (p18-19): top-only 0.0123 sq in = 136, 0.3 = 84, 1 sq in (645 sq mm) = 66 C/W - agreeing with AMS's 1000 sq mm -> 65, though all TI's numbers sit in section 9, which TI opens (p14) by disclaiming as "not part of the TI component specification". TI's two-sided rows are a DIFFERENT experiment: their split totals (0.132, 0.35, 0.568, 0.784, 1.0 sq in) are exactly AN-1028 layouts 12-16, whose boards carry 0.02 in plated vias (p8). No contradiction - TI SPLITS a fixed budget (Fig 9-11 ranks Top Cu best), AMS ADDS back-side area under a fixed top pour (~5 C/W). At TA 50 C even 55 C/W caps near 1.36 W: the envelope's 1.5 W marks where this record stops, never a licence.
